title: The Use of a β-lactamase-based Conductimetric Biosensor Assay to Detect Biomolecular Interactions
protocol: Produce and purify the hybrid protein BlaP-cAb-Lys3.
Store the protein in 50 mM phosphate buffer pH 7.4 with specified salt composition.
Fix the pH of the solution to 7.4 before adjusting the final volume to 1 L.
Filter sterilize the protein solution.
Dissolve 100 mg of HEWL in 10 mL of PBS.
Sterilize the HEWL solution by filtration using filters with a 0.22 μm cutoff.
Prepare 50 mM PBS as specified.
Adjust pH to 7.4 with HCl or NaOH before adjusting volume to 1 L.
Filter sterilize and store the PBS at 4°C.
Dissolve 3 g of casein hydrolysate in 100 mL of prepared PBS to make saturation/blocking solution.
Filter sterilize and store the saturation/blocking solution at 4°C.
Dissolve 1 g of casein hydrolysate in 100 mL of prepared PBS to make binding solution.
Filter sterilize and store the binding solution at 4°C.
Add 100 μL of Tween 20 (100%) in 100 mL of PBS to prepare a washing solution (0.1% Tween - PBS).
Store the washing solution at 4°C.
Add 1 mL of Triton X-100 (100%) in 100 mL of PBS to prepare an electrode preparation solution (1% Triton X-100 - PBS).
Store the electrode preparation solution at 4°C.
Dissolve 26 g of KCl in distilled water to a final volume of 100 mL to prepare an electrode regeneration solution (3.5 M KCl).
Filter sterilize and store the electrode regeneration solution at 4°C.
Dissolve 0.29 g of NaCl in distilled water to a final volume of 1 L to prepare a 5 mM NaCl solution.
Filter sterilize and store the 5 mM NaCl solution at 4°C.
Dissolve 26.7 mg of benzylpenicillin in 20 mL of 5 mM NaCl solution to prepare a detection solution (4 mM benzylpenicillin).
Filter sterilize and store the detection solution at -20°C.
Wash the electrodes by dipping into wells containing 300 μL of electrode preparation solution (1% Triton X-100 - PBS).
Perform each wash for 2 min with gentle mixing at room temperature.
Repeat the washing step three times.
Rinse the electrodes by dipping into wells containing 300 μL of distilled water.
Mix gently for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Regenerate the electrodes by dipping into wells containing 300 μL of regeneration solution (3.5 M KCl).
Allow regeneration overnight at 4 °C or for 1 hour at room temperature.
Perform 3 washes of the electrodes by dipping the tips into wells of a 96-well plate containing 300 µL/well of phosphate buffer saline.
Incubate each wash for 2 minutes with gentle mixing at room temperature.
Deposit a 15 μl drop of 40 µg/ml HEWL prepared in PBS onto the electrode surface.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C or 1 hour at room temperature.
Perform three washes of the electrodes with phosphate buffer saline by dipping the electrode parts into wells containing 300 µL/well of phosphate buffer saline.
Incubate each wash for 2 minutes with gentle mixing at room temperature.
Add a 50 μl drop of blocking solution onto the electrode surface.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Perform three washes as previously described by dipping the electrodes into wells containing phosphate buffer saline.
Dilute the BlaP-cAb-Lys3 solution to 20 µg/mL in binding solution.
Apply a 15 μL drop of the diluted BlaP-cAb-Lys3 solution onto the electrodes.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash three times using the wash solution.
Rinse the electrode once with PBS.
Plug the sensor chip via the copper-circuitry part to a digital multimeter.
Apply a 50 μL drop of detection solution onto the positive electrodes.
Apply a 50 μL drop of NaCl 5 mM solution onto the negative electrodes.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Monitor the conductance with a digital multimeter.
